text:
ops_alex: Heads up — we're seeing a thundering-herd style surge of concurrent cache misses against the hosted KV cache in us-west-2. Users reporting elevated tail latency and intermittent 5xx from the adapter.
sre_jamie: Confirmed. eviction_rate up ~4x on cache-pool-3, connection queueing on the proxy. Correlation with a burst of large-batch requests from a single client shard.
statusbot: Incident created: INC-2026-382 — Hosted KV cache contention (us-west-2). Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-382
infra_oncall: Mitigations in progress: enabling conservative prefix-level dedupe and request coalescing (kv.dedupe_prefix=true) across us-west-2 proxies. Also scaling proxy pool by +3 nodes while we stabilize.
eng_runtime: Rolling restart of cache-proxy with new config now. Commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n hosting-usw2 rollout restart deploy/cache-proxy
redis-cli -h cache-pool-3 INFO stats | grep evicted_keys
```
eng_runtime: Watching metrics — eviction_rate trending down after restart, but we still see hotspots on a few prefixes.
product_ops: Flagging top 10 customers on priority watch. Preparing a short customer note in case escalation needed. No public status update yet until we have mitigation results.
cs_olivia: Notifying impacted customers (top-tier) with template. Confirmed: no data loss — this is cache-only behavior.
sre_jamie: After config rollout + extra proxies, 5xx rate down ~70%, p99 latency reduced ~60%. We'll keep autoscaling enabled for 20m and observe.
ops_alex: Temporary additional guardrails: rate-limit large-batch calls at the edge (X-Client-Batch-Limit header enforced to 50), and enabled fallback-to-disk for cold prefixes to avoid backend thrash.
eng_runtime: Added alert: concurrent_cache_misses_per_prefix > 100 -> auto-enable dedupe and page oncall. I'll land the alert rule after this thread.
statusbot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-382 — Impact: Major degradation (partial recovery in progress).
cs_olivia: Customers asking timeline — telling them we're in monitoring with mitigations applied; follow-up ETA ~30–45m for full recovery verification.
product_ops: Postmortem owners assigned: jamie (SRE), alex (Ops), rachel (Eng Runtime). Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-thundering-herd
sre_jamie: Further steps planned: tune default TTLs for split-cache workloads, add prefix-level caching metrics, and implement client-side jitter recommendations in SDK docs.
ops_alex: Summary: root cause = synchronized cold prefixes + bursty large-batch requests -> thundering herd. Mitigations = coalescing/dedupe, scaling proxies, rate limits, disk-fallback. Current status = mitigated; monitoring for 60m. Will file full incident report once we collect logs/metrics. :white_check_mark:
eng_runtime: I'll follow up with PR for the alert rule and a config change to make dedupe opt-out rather than opt-in.
cs_olivia: Keeping CS looped and ready to escalate if customers report regressions. :thumbsup:
sre_jamie: Leaving thread open until we confirm stable for 1h. If anything new pops, ping here
